description: The name maps of Haspelmath's chapter on Standard Average European, with what its prose reports of the eastern Indo-European languages.

ContributionTable.Name: Maps 107.1-107.13
ContributionTable.Description: The languages of the name maps and the side of each line they lie on.
ContributionTable.comment: Read from 500 dpi page images, and the side of each solid line checked by flood-filling the image from outside, with each label located by OCR.

ContributionTable.Name: section 2
ContributionTable.Description: What the prose of section 2 reports of the eastern Indo-European languages, which the maps do not cover but for Armenian.

LanguageTable.Name: Armenian
LanguageTable.comment: Glottolog has Armenic as a family and Eastern and Western Armenian as languages; the chapter says only Armenian.

LanguageTable.Name: Komi
LanguageTable.comment: Glottolog has Komi as a family; the chapter says only Komi.

LanguageTable.Name: Mari
LanguageTable.comment: Glottolog has Mari as a family; the chapter says only Mari.

LanguageTable.Name: Mordvin
LanguageTable.comment: Glottolog has Mordvin as a family; the chapter says only Mordvin.

LanguageTable.Name: Nenets
LanguageTable.comment: Glottolog has Nenets as a family; the chapter says only Nenets.

LanguageTable.Name: Saami
LanguageTable.comment: Glottolog has Saami as a family. The chapter defines the western Uralic languages as Hungarian and Balto-Finnic (section 1), which leaves Saami with the others.

LanguageTable.Name: Sardinian
LanguageTable.comment: Glottolog divides Sardinian into several languages under Southern Romance, and the chapter does not say which it means.

LanguageTable.Name: Iranian
LanguageTable.comment: The branch, as sections 2.1 and 2.8 speak of it.

LanguageTable.Name: Indic
LanguageTable.comment: The branch, as sections 2.1, 2.4 and 2.8 speak of it.

LanguageTable.Name: Kurdish
LanguageTable.comment: Glottolog has Kurdish as a family; the chapter says only Kurdish.

LanguageTable.Name: Baluchi
LanguageTable.comment: Glottolog has Balochic as a family; the chapter says only Baluchi.

LanguageTable.Name: Punjabi
LanguageTable.comment: Glottolog distinguishes Eastern and Western Panjabi; the code is of Eastern Panjabi.

ParameterTable.Name: branch
ParameterTable.Description: The genealogical groups the criteria of section 1 reason with, by the textbook classification; the chapter names most of them on p. 1493.

ParameterTable.Name: experiencer ratio
ParameterTable.Description: The ratio of inverting to generalizing experiential predicates that Map 107.4 prints beside each language.

ParameterTable.Name: anticausative percentage
ParameterTable.Description: The percentage of anticausative pairs that Map 107.6 prints beside each language.

ParameterTable.Name: printed score
ParameterTable.Description: The number Map 107.13 prints in the region of a language; it prints none outside its lines.
